_readme: Per-service detail text, shown in a small box under a subcategory label in an
organization's established wellness wheel. Plain text, English only, authored by
hand: there is no generator and nothing here is encrypted.
<irb_participant_id>  matches the survey column, e.g. YSP01
BOTH vocabularies are allowed: survey keys such as
sub_occupational_4 (Job training) and interview keys such
A key renders only if that organization already shows the service in its wheel,
and blank text renders nothing at all. Partial coverage is expected: an unwritten
service looks exactly as it does today, with no empty box.
Keep entries to roughly 25 words. The box is about four lines tall and scrolls
_example is inert because the loader only reads service_details. Copy an entry up
into service_details to make it live.

occupational.sub_occupational_4: Blue-collar tracks in construction, HVAC and culinary, with tools and certification fees covered.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: Paid 12-week placements at $15/hour, capped at 20 hours weekly during term time.

physical.wellness_physical_meals: Fruit, bread and cheese at every school workshop, sandwiches at apprenticeships, and full cooked meals at the end-of-cohort celebration, chosen as whole rather than processed foods.

intellectual.wellness_intellectual_social_justice: A social justice apprenticeship group presented on Bad Bunny's use of music for change; workshops also examine which professionalism norms are rooted in white supremacy.

occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: Apprenticeships pay a $200 stipend across the twelve-week program; City Summer Internship runs six to eight weeks for about forty girls at roughly $550 weekly.

financial.wellness_financial_stipend_empowerment: Paid alongside covered transport between school and placements, so earnings stay intact; a check-cashing worksheet and Eastern Bank IDs help students access their money.

physical.wellness_physical_fitness: The fitness center is open daily and staff actively incentivize members to use it; swim team and newly added baseball clinics give teens organized options.
physical.wellness_physical_nutrition: A Healthy Habits course pairs nutrition lessons with hands-on activities such as smoothie making, and a spring health and wellness fair covers diet, hygiene and simple self-checks.
physical.wellness_physical_movement: An adventure club ran last fall and a walking club follows this spring, taking teens out of the building on foot around Dorchester at no cost.

emotional.sub_emotional_3: An on-site social worker, supported by two clinical interns, is a direct resource for members needing behavioral or emotional support during the after-school day.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: STEM classes run alongside arts and music, and staff or groups of youth who take an interest in a subject can start a new class around it.
intellectual.sub_intellectual_2: Power Forward is the teen college and career prep program; sessions bring in outside professionals, including a certified clinician who ran an hour on mental health.
intellectual.wellness_intellectual_creative_arts: Art and music programming runs year-round, including a girls of color class within the art program and music therapy led by outside facilitators for younger members.

financial.sub_financial_3: Financial literacy sessions for teens run in partnership with Webster Bank, as part of its initiative to spread financial literacy across the Boston area.

social.sub_social_1: Teen Breakout starts this spring: ten weeks of separate girls' and boys' sessions with guest speakers, led by staff in their early twenties, closing with a spring fling.
social.sub_social_2: Families are invited in through the year for a family Thanksgiving, holiday celebrations and season kickoff events, held at the clubhouses for members and their relatives.
social.sub_social_3: The club runs its own Juneteenth celebration and joins wider neighborhood events, including Harbor Point's community Juneteenth festival, tabling or running activities when partners invite them.
social.wellness_social_youth_council: Keystone Club, for ages thirteen to eighteen, follows Boys and Girls Clubs of America pillars including leadership, community service and academic success, and runs its own service projects.
social.wellness_social_peer_mentoring: Keystone teens mentor Torch Club, its ten to thirteen year old counterpart, bringing younger members into Keystone activities and helping them with their own small projects.

environmental.sub_environmental_3: A small gardening class runs each spring: members plant seeds indoors and move them outside to the grass area beside the clubhouses.

spiritual.sub_spiritual_1: Yoga and other mindfulness-centered enrichments are optional, and the Zen Den is an open space members can use whenever they are having a difficult time.
spiritual.wellness_spiritual_mindfulness_embedded: Sensory corners sit in program areas and at large events, with fidgets, ear protection and lower-mobility alternatives, so an overstimulated member always has an option.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_2: A post-secondary team works with Bunker Hill, UMass Boston and Roxbury Community College, running Community Connect hubs on campus and monitoring grades with consent.

occupational.sub_occupational_1: Summer internships posted on Future Boss; the PIC funds community-based roles and handles onboarding and payroll so employers can focus on training.
occupational.sub_occupational_2: A career specialist sits in every Boston public high school, and coaching continues after placement, including mediating misunderstandings with new managers.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Career specialists in each Boston public high school help students build a first resume and understand what city employers look for.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Career-readiness programs at ABCD Boston and MassHire Downtown covering soft skills and personality assessments, plus ESL classes and tracks for youth with disabilities.

financial.sub_financial_1: Career coaches are trained in budgeting, taxes and monthly expenses, and refer young adults to the Roxbury Financial Empowerment Center for hands-on plans.
financial.sub_financial_2: Support completing the FAFSA correctly and finding scholarships, with the goal of graduating with as little debt as possible.
financial.sub_financial_3: Workshops for parents on saving for a home or college tuition, plus Financially Lit with The Possible Zone, aimed at young fathers.

social.sub_social_1: Community Connect pairs students with a mentor in the same major, matched by an interests survey, which raises on-time graduation rates.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Academic workshops run through the school year and intensively over the summer for middle schoolers, previewing the next grade's curriculum so students start the year ahead.
intellectual.sub_intellectual_2: Monthly workshops through the school year, plus a dedicated week when rising seniors work on college applications; support continues into college for as long as students want it.
intellectual.sub_intellectual_3: After-school support during the school year for students who need it, which in practice often takes the form of tutoring in current coursework.
intellectual.wellness_intellectual_creative_arts: Arts and crafts clubs and project-based classes run through summer programming, where creative work is most concentrated; high school Saturdays include free time for crafts and board games.

occupational.sub_occupational_1: A high school intern program for underclassmen and Junior Teacher roles for upperclassmen leading in classrooms, plus a database of Boston jobs and programs out of state and abroad.
occupational.sub_occupational_2: Post-secondary advisors hold one-on-one check-ins with college students and alumni on job searching and salary negotiation; a February or April break each year is given to career exploration.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Resumes are workshopped on Super Saturdays, the roughly six monthly high school sessions where students also sit down and apply for jobs on the spot.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: Rising ninth graders in the summer Leadership Academy are paid at the end of the season for campus leadership: peer mentoring, helping at snack, interning for a day.
occupational.wellness_occupational_mock_interviews: Practice interviews sit inside the monthly high school career and college exploration curriculum, giving students a rehearsal before the applications they submit in the same sessions.

financial.sub_financial_1: High school is where money conversations start: how to save a first paycheck and what to do with it, as students begin earning through summer positions.
financial.sub_financial_2: Workshops on scholarships such as Posse and QuestBridge, plus a financial aid calculator that helps students work out what a college award letter actually means.
financial.sub_financial_3: Students vote on choice workshop topics; a recent one covered taxes and their effect on a paycheck, and others cover talking with family about what college costs.
financial.wellness_financial_emergency_fund: The Bridge the Gap Fund covers emergency costs once students reach college: a replacement laptop, a semester of books, or a small gap between aid and tuition.

physical.wellness_physical_fitness: Middle schoolers run with Soul Train at Trinity Boston Connects, which supplies a year-long facilitation guide, and train with the Soccer Unity Project through the summer.
physical.wellness_physical_nutrition: Conversations about quick, healthy choices and cooking rotations with middle schoolers build practical eating skills; nutrition programming is still being built out.
physical.wellness_physical_meals: Young people are fed every day at both the South End elementary site and the Lower Roxbury middle school site.
physical.wellness_physical_movement: A daily health and wellness rotation gets everyone moving; elementary groups head to nearby parks to run, use the playground and play on the basketball court.

emotional.wellness_emotional_check_ins: Weekly social-emotional-spiritual care rotations open with a check-in on how everyone is feeling; teens also submit a Thursday checkout form to the teen director.
emotional.wellness_emotional_clinical_referral: Referrals and references to outside providers when a young person needs licensed counseling beyond what the program's own social worker and chaplain offer.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Rotations are planned around learning objectives and critical thinking questions from the Five C's of Youth Development, each closing with a short reflection on what it sparked.
intellectual.sub_intellectual_2: An annual bridge trip tours HBCUs and campuses teens picked for fit; a recent session had them role-play an admissions team weighing what colleges actually look for.
intellectual.wellness_intellectual_social_justice: Racial equity and cultural humility are built into lesson planning across programs, alongside violence prevention grounded in restorative rather than punitive responses.

occupational.sub_occupational_2: College and career programming runs through the teen program, with the goal that every teen leaves with a clear post-secondary plan; 100% graduate each year.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Family programs are built as one- or two-year jobs that develop workforce skills toward stronger employment, with a staff social worker adding workforce development support for parents.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: Teens hired after ninth grade work about ten hours a week in the out-of-school-time programs, nine on site plus a weekly training or staff meeting.

financial.wellness_financial_emergency_fund: Partner churches drop off bags of groceries and grocery store gift cards once or twice a week for families, with bags tailored to be culturally respectful.
financial.wellness_financial_stipend_empowerment: Ninth graders who finish the middle school program earn a stipend for a first job experience built around community volunteering, leadership training and the organization's podcast.

social.sub_social_2: A parent program places about 42 parents as trained classroom aides in Boston Public Schools, running in English, Spanish, Somali and Haitian Creole.
social.sub_social_3: Step-up days bring the oldest elementary groups over to the middle school site for shared celebrations, such as a Black Excellence Month event.
social.wellness_social_peer_mentoring: Younger participants are supported by teen staff who came up through the same programs, several of whom have been part of St. Stephen's since first grade.

emotional.sub_emotional_1: Therapy groups for young people in detention and in the community, including a therapeutic sports group on one detention unit and a group at a Charlestown education program.
emotional.sub_emotional_2: Outreach begins in the aftermath of an arrest or an incident of community violence, with referrals from the Boston Police Department, schools, hospitals and juvenile detention centers.
emotional.sub_emotional_3: Free individual therapy from trained social workers, with no insurance billing and no cap on how long a family is served; sessions happen in homes, schools, hospitals or detention.
emotional.wellness_emotional_trauma_informed: Ongoing training from trauma specialists keeps therapy informal and relational for youth who would not otherwise engage; tools include sand tray and an EMDR protocol being adapted for community settings.
emotional.wellness_emotional_clinical_referral: Referrals to in-home or outpatient therapy, psychological and neuropsychological testing, and DMH applications; social workers file the paperwork, sit with parents at appointments and bring youth to evaluations.

occupational.sub_occupational_3: A social worker builds a first resume with a young person from babysitting, painting or yard work, then accompanies them to the interview and can provide professional clothing.

social.sub_social_1: A social worker walks the young person into an after-school center, basketball team or Boston Center for Youth and Families, handles the introductions, and follows up so a positive adult sticks.
social.sub_social_2: One referral brings in the whole household: parents connected to employment, medical or mental health care, younger siblings to camp, and help navigating school, hospital and legal systems.

spiritual.sub_spiritual_1: Mindfulness and meditation are worked into the group sessions run on the detention units and at the Charlestown education program.
spiritual.wellness_spiritual_mindfulness_embedded: The same mindfulness practices carry into one-to-one sessions, and spirituality is explored further when a young person chooses to raise it.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Workshops run regularly and are often outsourced to partners such as the Mirror Project, including Know Your Rights sessions where youth can ask immigration questions directly.
intellectual.sub_intellectual_2: A career services manager sits with each young person on school applications, joins campus site visits, and coordinates meetings with staff at the institution.

occupational.sub_occupational_2: Each young person is paired with a youth development or career services manager and meets weekly, planning the move into employment beyond More Than Words.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Readiness is a six-to-twelve-week introductory program every new young person completes, building the professionalism, punctuality and dress-code habits the job itself will expect.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: Young people hold two jobs: a business job in the retail shop, trucks or online bookstore, and a You job working toward personal goals.

financial.sub_financial_1: Managers build a budget with the young person when support tapers off, for example covering a first month of phone service and planning the handover.
financial.sub_financial_2: Career services managers sit with young people to complete the FAFSA, part of the same one-on-one help offered when applying to college or training programs.
financial.sub_financial_3: Financial trainings are largely outsourced to expert partners, with banks running sessions on checking versus savings accounts and which products suit a given young person.
financial.wellness_financial_emergency_fund: Just in Time Funds cover urgent needs like a bus pass, a bed or groceries, and grocery gift cards went to every young person when SNAP lapsed.

social.wellness_social_youth_council: Changemakers brings youth together each year to change organizational policy directly; one group rewrote the attendance policy, including how tallies and strikes work.

physical.wellness_physical_fitness: Twenty-three Olympic-style sports, free and open to youth with and without disabilities, each with a six-to-eight-week introductory clinic and a competitive arm that travels to other cities.
physical.wellness_physical_nutrition: Most program sites offer healthy snacks alongside food knowledge resources: pointers to local food pantries, guidance on daily water intake, and basic nutrition charts.
physical.wellness_physical_movement: Young Athletes develops fine and gross motor skills for ages two to seven. Train for Life is a twelve-week strength and conditioning program built with Vanderbilt University clinicians.

social.sub_social_2: Take-home activity materials in several languages let families run the program at home when they cannot get to a site. Parent and community leadership groups guide neighborhood outreach.
social.sub_social_3: Unified bowling nights, open houses, pizza parties, movie nights, joint volunteer projects and dances at the summer games and state competitions, for people with and without disabilities.
social.wellness_social_peer_mentoring: Athletes are paired with neurotypical partners on rosters split evenly, with volunteer team escorts at competitions and, in some programs, accountability buddies who check in between practices.

emotional.sub_emotional_1: An eight-week Caregivers healing cohort for youth and women affected by incarceration or community harm; members support one another, then graduate into a mentor phase.
emotional.sub_emotional_2: After a shooting nearby, separate youth and adult teams run healing circles in the affected area, three following one recent Roxbury incident, plus door-to-door flyers.
emotional.sub_emotional_3: Counseling is delivered on site by a lead clinician and a staff of clinicians, open to youth and to families connected through our programs.
emotional.wellness_emotional_trauma_informed: Facilitators follow a guide developed with a consulting doctor, saying community harm rather than homicide, and refresh it in workshops run with the City of Boston.
emotional.wellness_emotional_clinical_referral: Referrals reach our clinicians from the Boston Police Department and the City of Boston, and families are connected onward to partner organizations for services we do not run.

occupational.sub_occupational_2: Facilitators ask which fields interest youth, map college and technical-school routes, and bring in local professionals, a hair salon owner for instance, to talk about that work.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Resume workshops sit inside the youth mentorship program, alongside professionalism and career-advancement sessions, so participants finish the cohort with a resume in hand.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Job-sustainability workshops cover workplace responsibilities, raising a problem with a manager, presentation do's and don'ts, and norms such as phone use during a shift.

emotional.sub_emotional_2: Triggered by repeating patterns rather than one-off incidents, such as a young person disengaging from learning; staff work with school social workers to confirm the concern appears in more than one setting.
emotional.wellness_emotional_clinical_referral: Staff refer families to outside professionals sourced through schools, parents and partner meetings, including a Haitian psychiatrist for the center's large Haitian community and a partner organization that makes home visits.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Free computer classes run from the site's computer center, open to teens and to their parents, since the program extends its services to whole families.

occupational.sub_occupational_1: High school students who need community service hours for a course requirement can complete them on site at Georgetowne.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Free resume writing for teens and for their parents, with staff also available to help families through summer job applications.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Career exploration and job training workshops for teens, backed by guest speakers from different professions, including an attorney last year and a further lineup this year.

financial.sub_financial_3: A mostly online course covering saving, opening a bank account and writing a check, with a certificate on completion; staff also pass on the Boston Public Schools family savings account.

social.sub_social_1: In-house mentoring is informal, built through years of relationship with staff; more formal mentoring matches are usually arranged through the young person's school.
social.sub_social_3: Weekly social activities open to all ages, from dance to health sessions to college visits, plus community events that whole families are invited to attend.
social.wellness_social_youth_council: A youth council running several years gives teens of any age a place to raise needs; staff hear every side before decisions and coach youth to advocate for themselves.

physical.wellness_physical_fitness: Quarterly wellness retreats where yoga and similar practices are led by hired specialists, with girls suggesting facilitators they have enjoyed and helping shape what each retreat includes.
physical.wellness_physical_movement: When weather allows, retreats move outdoors for field-day activities such as jump rope and hand games, and the group also joins organized walks together.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Workshops built on an in-house curriculum, including All About Self-Love, where girls define themselves on their own terms; activities are tried with girls and revised on their feedback.
intellectual.sub_intellectual_2: Belonging and Becoming Fellows attend monthly workshops on the application process and what campus life will ask of them, plus one-on-one meetings for college essay feedback.
intellectual.wellness_intellectual_social_justice: Every program is rooted in social justice and identity development, giving girls language for criminalization and adultification and the skills to question the systems behind them.

occupational.sub_occupational_1: One or two interns are hosted each semester and supported across the full term by the staff team.
occupational.sub_occupational_2: Girls spend time with local Black and Brown professional women who volunteer to talk through their careers and the paths that took them there.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Fellows build resumes and LinkedIn profiles alongside their college-access workshops, with networking practice folded into the same sessions.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: High school girls are hired as counselors at the organization's summer camp, a paid part-time role for older participants.

financial.sub_financial_2: Fellowship workshops walk through the financial aid process, and fellows can book one-on-one meetings to make sense of an aid package before deciding.
financial.sub_financial_3: Partner organizations run sessions on bank accounts, credit cards and everyday money decisions, so girls can weigh choices that fit their own circumstances.

social.sub_social_1: Staff sit down with girls to problem-solve school and home situations as they arise, coaching self-advocacy; check-ins continue after graduation, with gatherings when college students are home.
social.sub_social_3: Events grounded in being in community with each other, paired with workshops on healthy relationships, boundaries and communication; girls help decide what each event looks like.

intellectual.wellness_intellectual_creative_arts: Semester-long hands-on programs in songwriting, performance and instrumental music, plus production, videography, engineering and a youth-powered low-power FM radio station; groups meet two to four hours weekly on shared projects.

occupational.sub_occupational_1: Medium-specific internships follow the introductory sound or video class, moving youth into paid gig work in that field, with an abundant number of gigs to opt into.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Part of the weekly professional-development session for Leaders in Training, the paid youth cohort who co-facilitate Zumix programs.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Sound engineering learned in programs becomes a working skill: youth run live sound for the community groups and artists who perform in Zumix's space.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: A summer jobs program with the City of Boston and the City of Revere places about 20 young people in 20 to 25 hour weeks of cohort learning and concert-series support.

social.sub_social_2: Community arts events are deliberately all-ages, keeping families connected to their young people's work; recent examples include a dance film screening and a Mother's Day concert.
social.sub_social_3: An outdoor concert series runs in Pierce Park each summer, open to everyone and often how neighbors first meet Zumix; other community groups also program events in Zumix's space.
social.wellness_social_youth_council: Teen Council brings together youth from across Zumix's programs, meeting every Friday to plan community arts events, advise staff on organizational questions, and propose projects of their own.
social.wellness_social_peer_mentoring: Every program pairs an adult co-facilitator with a youth co-facilitator from the Leaders in Training cohort, who design the agenda and curriculum together.

physical.wellness_physical_nutrition: Visiting facilitators run meal-prep workshops on putting together a lunch and managing meals around an 8:30 start, since some worksites have no restaurant nearby.
physical.wellness_physical_meals: Breakfast and lunch are provided for the first few weeks of the program, continuing until a member receives their first stipend payment.
physical.wellness_physical_movement: A visiting facilitator runs sessions on simple exercises and stretching that members can keep up on their own to stay in shape.

emotional.sub_emotional_1: Weekly opt-in men's and women's groups meet on site after program hours, the men's with City of Boston's Black Male Advancement; members may attend either.
emotional.sub_emotional_2: Members in crisis are connected to city resources including the Trauma Team and the 311 line, matched to whichever specialist agency fits the situation.
emotional.wellness_emotional_clinical_referral: Set on a Roxbury healthcare and academic campus, the program connects interested members to mental health services there, with support staff helping make the calls.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Workshops and trainings carry industry-recognized certifications: OSHA, CPR and first aid, a Sherwin-Williams painting credential, GPRO building decarbonization, and a two-day statewide PREVENT de-escalation certificate.

occupational.sub_occupational_1: Phase two members complete a six-month internship with one of our employer partners, ideally hired on by that partner at the end of it.
occupational.sub_occupational_2: A four-month exploratory phase exposes members to green-industry lines of work to test fit; a workforce development team then connects members to their next employer.
occupational.sub_occupational_3: Advancing past phase one requires a completed PowerCorps-standard resume, built with a certified career coach who also flags details like an unprofessional email address.
occupational.sub_occupational_4: Phase two specializes in one of three tracks: urban forestry with a horticulture focus, arboriculture and tree care, or building operations for energy-efficient commercial buildings.
occupational.wellness_occupational_stipend: Members receive roughly $1,100 every two weeks, above minimum wage, plus a monthly T pass, PowerCorps gear and composite-toe boots.
occupational.wellness_occupational_mock_interviews: At least three rounds with volunteer employer partners in panel, online and one-to-one formats, scored out of twenty on preparation, posture, handshake and eye contact.

financial.sub_financial_2: Staff assist with FAFSA applications, and as an AmeriCorps program every member earns a Segal Education Award for their time in the program.

environmental.sub_environmental_1: Members learn to name local parks, tree species and invasive plants, and study heat island effect and building decarbonization, often applying it at home.
environmental.sub_environmental_2: Neighborhood beautification crews remove invasive species, plant and prune, build and maintain trails, and repair and paint park benches.

intellectual.sub_intellectual_1: Sessions on Massachusetts state financial aid (MASFA), covering eligibility rules many immigrant families do not know about, so youth can apply for aid and pursue college.

financial.sub_financial_2: Guidance on accessing Massachusetts state financial aid, offered through trusted community channels by staff of African and Caribbean descent, with college enrollment tracked afterwards.
financial.wellness_financial_stipend_empowerment: Participants in the six-week summer African Storytelling Program clock 20 hours weekly and are paid about $1,800 each, funded by the City of Boston.

social.sub_social_3: Gatherings open to all ages, bringing together families of shared cultural background, including a final showcase where African Storytelling Program participants present their group projects.
